A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same TRIRL research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, algorithms and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original grid-world, MuJoCo and robot imitation experiments, reward retraining and transfer tests, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, transfer evaluations and appendix sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, reward correction, the discriminator buffer and policy-update variants are unchanged. Appendix B newly explains encoder training for the feature-based variant already used in v1 Section 5.1; this documents the existing procedure without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same grid-world, five MuJoCo locomotion benchmarks, Go2/G1 tasks, motion-capture demonstrations and transfer scenarios involving Point Maze, Ant and Half Cheetah. The added explanation of SFM's restricted coverage introduces no evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: GAIL, AIRL, AMP, LSIQ and NEAR in the main benchmarks; SFM in Table 2; and AIRL and NEAR in the transfer comparison. The new captions explain existing SFM omissions rather than removing it from a comparison.

E3.justification: Table 7 revises the reported optimal epsilon range from 0.45–0.75 to 0.2–0.4. This changes a documented experimental hyperparameter range, but the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other evaluation settings and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, discriminator sensitivity analysis, training-stability plots, demonstration and buffer-size sweeps, beta/epsilon ablations, transfer tests and reward visualization are retained. The expanded feature-encoder explanation adds no analysis or experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 independent seeds in Section 5 and 95% confidence intervals in Table 3. The uncertainty displays and information about independently initialized retraining runs are unchanged.

E6.justification: Benchmark, retraining/transfer, runtime, memory and ablation results are unchanged, including their plotted curves. For example, Table 3 retains IQM values of 0.7881 for TRIRL max eta and 0.3297 for GAIL. Table 7's revised epsilon range concerns settings rather than a new performance result.

T1.justification: The stated reverse-KL guarantee in Section 3 now concerns progress toward the entropy-regularized expert occupancy instead of the expert occupancy. This qualifies the mathematical guarantee, while the objective, Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2 and Appendix A derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the claimed occupancy improvement to the entropy-regularized expert target. The central TRIRL contribution, global reward and transfer claims, and abstract's 2.4x aggregate-performance claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Table 2 newly explains that evaluating SFM on Go2/G1 would require substantial engineering and is left for future work. Table 3 explicitly explains SFM's exclusion from the aggregate comparison because it was evaluated only on MuJoCo. These additions clarify existing comparison limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix B now specifies feature-encoder training through energy prediction and denoising score matching on perturbed expert samples. Table 7 adds tuning recommendations and revises epsilon's range. The future code/dataset release promise becomes a statement that code and supplementary material are available through a project link; linked contents cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Peters et al. (2010), Relative Entropy Policy Search, as a reference supporting Fact A.3. It also revises the related-work description of IQ-Learn's policy construction to describe an approximation using its closed-form relationship to the Q-function. Broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: There are localized wording revisions, expanded appendix explanations, updated release information and acknowledgements, and small spelling edits. The explicit trajectory-expectation formula is shortened to a verbal description. Section organization and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 7 expands from two to three columns, adds tuning recommendations and groups parameters by max-eta and TR-loss variants. Tables 2–3 receive longer captions with corresponding spacing shifts. Figures and result-table structures otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision and reproducibility by qualifying the occupancy guarantee, explaining feature-encoder training, clarifying SFM's comparison scope and adding practical tuning guidance and access information. The empirical evidence and proofs are retained. The epsilon revision is unexplained and linked resources are unverified locally, so these changes support a limited documentation and clarity improvement.
